sense.text:
Today’s class is called Apollos Creed. Apollo Creed is the character in the Rocky movies, the fighter who picked out Rocky, a no-name fighter, just to have somebody to beat up; Rocky took advantage of the moment, lost the first time and came back again. The name comes from what is known as the Apostles Creed, and the Apostles Creed is believing in the Trinity, God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Spirit, used by the Catholic Church, the Lutherans, the Anglicans, the Presbyterians, the Methodists and the rest of the denominations. Look at the pictures they put with it: that ain’t no apostles in the Bible. The class is a play on that word, because of the brother Apollos.

Some of y’all reading the scriptures might not even have read about this brother. There’s not that much on him, but what you read about him makes you intrigued, makes you try to figure out what this brother was really about.

“A certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures”: right away they’re telling you this brother Apollos was mighty in the scriptures. That’s how we have to be.

“This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit”. Fervent means fire: he was burning in the spirit, zealous, he had zeal. He was fired up to go out there and teach. When you read, you’ve got to understand what you’re reading. So not only was he an eloquent man, good in the scriptures, but he was fervent in the spirit; he was going out there going crazy teaching the people, the same way John the Revelator says he was in the spirit on the Lord’s day.

“He spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.” This is important. By this time the disciples had already been rolling with Christ, and Christ was already dead. So he was teaching, but teaching knowing only the baptism of John: he knew about the water baptism, the baptism where you had to confess your sins. That’s what sends us to Matthew 3, to see what John’s baptism was.

“In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judea, And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” “For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet”: this was already talked about in the book of Isaiah. John is fulfilling a prophecy that was written way back, and that’s what he’s bringing out here. In the spirit he’s saying, I’m preparing the way of the Lord.

Who John the Baptist was is part of what Apollos knew. What tribe was John the Baptist from? The tribe of Levi. The scriptures say prove all things, so when we’re asked what tribe John is from, we are supposed to be able to prove it, and the proof is that his father was a priest. Y’all have to know these things; this is the stuff that Apollos knew.

“And the same John had his raiment of camel’s hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey.” John the Baptist only ate locusts and wild honey; that was his diet. You can eat certain locusts, certain insects, and you can’t eat certain insects; y’all find that out in Leviticus 11.

“Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judea, and all the region round about Jordan, And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins.” Confessing their sins: this is what John the Baptist was about. When John had people out there getting baptized, he wasn’t an idiot like today’s church, taking the people, come on in, and as soon as you go in the water the lady starts singing and there’s some drama. No. You had to confess something; you couldn’t come playing games. He’s not just taking people and dunking them in the water. You had to come forth and say, I committed adultery, I’m a thief, I’m a murderer. You had to say all of that, and then you got baptized in the water.

This is what Apollos was teaching. He was mighty in the scriptures.

precepts.why:
This is the prophecy John the Baptist was bringing out in the book of Matthew. “Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God. Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem”. Speak comfortably means let Jerusalem know what it is they must do to repent, showing them the law and all of that. That’s what comfort is: the comfort of the scriptures.

“That her warfare is accomplished” means the Lord said, all right, I’m done with your punishment, “for she hath received of the Lord’s hand double for all her sins.”

Then the very words Matthew quotes: “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.” “Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain: And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.” As you can see, John in Matthew 3 is fulfilling that prophecy: he is the voice in the wilderness preparing the way of the Lord.

The proof that John the Baptist was of the tribe of Levi: his father was a priest. “There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia”. All the priests had a certain time they had to be in the temple; his course was the course of Abia, the eighth course, like it talks about in Chronicles, meaning he was dealing with the incense.

“And his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth. And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years. And it came to pass, that while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his course”: a priest of the course, and a wife of the daughters of Aaron.

“But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.” That’s John the Baptist, the son of the priest Zacharias, so he is of Levi.

John the Baptist and Christ were cousins, and that’s in Luke chapter 1 as well when you read on. Y’all have to know these things. This is the stuff that Apollos knew, quick like that.

sense.text: “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”. You’ve got to come and repent from your sins, and then bring forth the fruits of the spirit. That’s why John said bring forth fruits meet for repentance: fruits good for repentance. That’s what meet means. You’ve got to know all these precepts and know how to explain all this.

“And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.” Why is he saying don’t think you have Abraham to your father? Don’t boast, don’t puff yourself up, because God can raise up Abraham descendants just like that. And why use Abraham? Because through him came the promise: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. But Abraham had other children too, and that’s what Romans 9 opens up.

It can’t be that the Lord came for everybody, because it says don’t say that you have Abraham to your father. This is where the promises came.

precepts.why:
What the fruits are: “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.”

This is what you’ve got to bring forth. You’ve got to come and repent from your sins, and then these are the fruits of the spirit. That’s why John said “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”: fruits good for repentance.

sense.text: Romans 9 is a beautiful chapter for an Israelite. “For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh: Who are Israelites”. My kinsmen, my brethren according to the flesh, who are Israelites: Paul is an Israelite. The whole top of this chapter is talking about the bloodline, who the Israelites are, “to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises”.

“Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came”. That means Christ came for the Israelites. Simple, that’s it. Of whom, according to the flesh, Christ came: Christ came for Israel, period. When you’re out there teaching, you can’t ever stumble on that.

“Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.” Abraham had other kids; just because they’re of the seed of Abraham doesn’t mean the promises are for them all. It tells you in Isaac: he was talking specifically about Isaac. But at the end of the day the scriptures say prove all things. You can say whatever sounds good, but where’s the proof that Abraham had other children and the promise wasn’t theirs? Precept must be upon precept.

“That is, They which are the children of the flesh”. All those other kids of Abraham are the children of the flesh. It’s worded like this because they want you to understand what Paul is talking about when he says in the flesh. “These are not the children of God”: they’re not the children of God, although they are of Abraham’s flesh. “But the children of the promise are counted for the seed.”

That’s how you have precept upon precept: you’re able to prove what it is you’re saying.

precepts.why:
The proof that Abraham had other children who were not the promised seed. “Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah. And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.” Then the sons of Jokshan, of Dedan and of Midian: “All these were the children of Keturah.”

“And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac.” He had all those sons, and he gave all that he had to Isaac. Watch this: “But unto the sons of the concubines, which Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son”. They were all his sons, but he gave them gifts and sent them away.

Abraham was rich, so he gave his sons some stuff and they went out, when they were able to take care of themselves, and built. Gifts is what he gave them, not the inheritance. But Isaac, that’s a different story: you’re staying right here, you’re taking all that I’ve got. That is In Isaac shall thy seed be called. This Bible is the best.

It’s the same thing with the nations. “When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.” Israel had to get what they had to get, and everybody else got the gift.

The Lord created all the people, so he gave them lands, he gave them this and that. Y’all might be saying, look at the Arabs, they’ve got oil. The Lord gave them that, but he based it around the bounds of Israel. The same thing with Abraham: he had all these sons and gave them gifts, but the inheritance went to Isaac.

Reverse engineering the line. Y’all are going to bump into a lot of Christians and people defending different parts of the Bible for their religion, saying everybody can be saved, because that’s what’s been taught out there. When they read Romans 11 and different scriptures they don’t understand what it means. But it says in Isaac shall thy seed be called; the promise comes through Abraham’s line.

“And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram”: that’s Abraham right there; his name was later changed to Abraham. As you go up the chapter: Terah came from Nahor, Nahor came from Serug, Serug came from Reu, Reu came from Peleg, Peleg came from Eber, Eber came from Salah, Salah came from Arphaxad, and Arphaxad came from Shem. Shem is one of the three sons.

So what about Ham and Japheth? As far as the scriptures are concerned, Ham and Japheth have no shot; they have nothing to do with it. So it can’t be that the Lord came for everybody, because remember, it says don’t say that you have Abraham to your father; this is where the promises came. These other two lines are out. Everybody is out except for the Israelites.

You have to know those little details. When you’re discussing and trying to defend the faith you’re going to need them. You think they just put this one begat that one in there? It’s there for a reason. Write these notes down.

sense.text: “This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.” All of that, John’s baptism of confessing sins, Abraham’s seed, the bloodline, is what Apollos had in him as a man mighty in the scriptures.

“And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly”. When they heard Apollos they said, man, this guy’s strong, but he’s missing something. So they sat him down: brother, you’re something else, but do you know this? They told him about Christ; he didn’t know nothing about Christ, all he knew was John’s baptism. They sat him down and said, listen, this is what happened, this is the story. And Apollos didn’t say, listen, I know the scriptures already, you can’t tell me a damn thing. He received it, and he went out there and started teaching it.

“And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him”. He was so strong they said, listen, when Apollos comes through, take him; that brother is serious. “Who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace”.

“For he mightily convinced the Jews”. How do you convince somebody mightily if you’re not pulling out proof? If you’re just talking anything, that just sparks a thought. “And that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.” This past week it actually hit me right there: shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ. How many times have we actually done that, used the scriptures to prove that Christ was exactly who we say he is? This is what that brother was doing.

Was the New Testament available? No, it wasn’t. So he was using the Old Testament. If you were told right now to go into the Bible and prove publicly, mightily, by the scriptures that Jesus is the Christ, what would you pull out? You would have to go to Isaiah and Ezekiel, which have prophecies of Christ, and he’s in Psalms, he’s all over Genesis. That’s all Apollos could go on. That thing is heavy.

This is what Apollos was doing: he mightily convinced the Jews, publicly showing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ. How many times have we actually done that? The New Testament was not available; he was using the Old Testament. Put yourself there with a Bible that has only the Old Testament: what are you going to pull out of it to show Christ? You’d have to go to Isaiah, to Ezekiel, to the Psalms, to Genesis; he’s all over. That’s why we call this class Apollos Creed: Apollos was not playing, his game was detailed, he taught diligently and wasn’t letting nothing go. We have to get strong like that.

“He hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.” If you’ve never seen Christ, how would you be able to put Isaiah 53 with him? The ones who were there had to be shown the scriptures: listen, this is that man right here. Coming up we were thinking of that Jesus picture, and the women only like that because of the way the picture looks. Put up a man there with dark skin, a big guy, not comely, not good-looking at all: that’s what it says, no form nor comeliness, no beauty that we should desire him.

That’s why the Lord is a mastermind. He didn’t bring in nobody you were going to look at right away and say, that must be him. You had to hear it, you had to hear the spirit. That’s how the ones who were there were able to go into the Old Testament and say, oh, this must be him.

“He is despised and rejected of men”: who rejected him? You’ve got to know these answers, because the Christian church says none of the Jews or the Israelites listened to Christ and then he went to teaching the other nations. We ain’t going to hear all the lip service; we want the scripture. That’s what we learn in this school: break down the scriptures, not just to prove who Christ was but to prove that you’re the Israelites. You have to study it.

“Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.” Sum that up: how do you know this is talking about Christ? Before Christ came around, you couldn’t. When you read it in the time of Christ, after he got put to death, you’re going to say: oh, Christ got crucified, he was put to death for us, he said he’s going to take on all our sins. You wouldn’t be able to know that unless he went through it; then you see, this is what it’s talking about.

These are the scriptures Apollos was using to prove that Jesus was the Christ. We could just give you the answers and move on, but giving y’all the answers doesn’t work, because when we ask you again you don’t know. You’ve got to study to show yourself approved to God. People in the streets won’t come at you with the easy stuff; you can’t go out there doing push-ups and sit-ups and be useless on the street.

precepts.why: “And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.” This is who he’s rejected by: the elders, the chief priests and the scribes. They didn’t want to give up their leadership; they didn’t want to let Christ continue, because the people were going to follow him and they were going to lose their place and nation. That’s the answer from the scripture to who despised and rejected him.

sense.text:
Take Genesis 49 as an example. It breaks down the twelve tribes; we use it. But did the disciples back then know what it was talking about? When could Genesis 49 actually be taught? Remember the Lord showed the prophets things, but as far as the breakdown of Genesis 49, how would it be able to be explained if most of it didn’t happen yet?

“Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; and he shall be for an haven of ships”: it’s talking about the Panama Canal. It’s in the land of Zebulun, and it is the haven of ships. Before the Panama Canal was built, was this scripture able to be broken down? Did we know that was the tribe of Zebulun hanging out over there? No.

It’s the same with Isaiah 53. Y’all have got to start learning how to learn, how to process, and get the precept game in order; there are too many classes online for y’all to be clueless about what it’s talking about.

“Binding his foal unto the vine, and his ass’s colt unto the choice vine”: he’s binding his colt unto the choice vine. Just reading that, you don’t know what it’s talking about; you would have to know what happened with Christ to know it’s speaking of him. We have the New Testament now and can go to it and say, this is what it is. Before that they didn’t, so they were saying, remember when Christ came, and this is the scripture that proves it.

“His eyes shall be red with wine”: how is that proving that Jesus was the Christ? Apollos was pulling this out. We all thought it meant judgment, that he was angry with lasers coming out of his eyes. It means wine: he would drink wine and sit with the publicans.

“And his teeth white with milk”: that’s the milk of the word, Christ teaching, teaching, teaching.

This is how strong Apollos was. He had to pull all that out and prove it to the people: remember when he came with the foal of an ass, that’s what it said in Zechariah; remember Genesis 49 said his teeth would be white with milk, according to the word; remember his eyes red with wine, he would always drink wine and sit with the publicans. Some things we are not going to know for now. The disciples walked with him every day and didn’t understand. It’s no sin not to understand, but it’s not a good look when you’re not trying to find out.

precepts.why: “The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.” A winebibber is actual wine. His eyes red with wine is not judgment or anger; it is Christ eating and drinking with the publicans and sinners.

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. His teeth white with milk is the sincere milk of the word, because that’s what Christ was doing: teaching, teaching, teaching.

“Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.” This goes with binding his ass’s colt unto the choice vine. Just reading it you don’t know what it is talking about; you would have to know what happened with Christ in order to know this is speaking about him.

“All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet”: “Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.” Here is where it actually happened, written down in the New Testament as the fulfilment of Zechariah.

“Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt. These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.”

That’s excellent: these things understood not his disciples at the first. It was afterwards that they said, I remember that in Zechariah, he fits that. That’s how Apollos proved it to the people: remember when he came on the foal of an ass? That’s what it said in Zechariah.

sense.text:
“I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee”: the Lord is telling Moses this. Whose brethren? The Israelites. Like unto thee: like Moses. So what was Moses’ job? He delivered the children of Israel out of Egypt, he followed all the commandments, he taught and gave the commandments. Who else came around like Moses? Find out Moses’ job and his duties, then think who else came around that was like him.

Moses was the mediator between the children of Israel and God, and the other one who came as a mediator is Christ. It means nobody is going to go to the Father without Christ.

What exactly was being mediated? The sins are committed, and Moses handed down the laws and the judgment: listen, y’all are out of order, this is what has to be done. They repented, they did the sacrifices, and that was the mediation to the Lord. Now Christ came and there’s no animal sacrifice, but still we’ve got to repent through Christ. That’s what it means that he was raised up like unto Moses, and this is a scripture used to prove that Jesus was the Christ. It is a lot, and you’ve got to learn it.

You can’t just sit there learning; you have to take what you learn and apply it when these questions come. Even if you only teach one or two people, you’ve got to have a couple of bullets.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: that’s talking about Christ. Then it says he shall be called “The mighty God, The everlasting Father”. What does that mean? Answers about the Trinity, him and his father being the same, don’t settle it; we have to get these scriptures.

Christ literally created the things; the Most High gave him the blueprint and Christ did the work. That’s why he’s being called the everlasting Father, because he created us. The Most High is called the Most High God; the Most High created Christ, and then Christ had to do his job.

We go to John 1 to prove why Christ is called the everlasting Father. “In the beginning was the Word”: what is the precept for the Word? If you don’t know what the Word is, you cannot understand this chapter at all; it’s impossible. This is basic, and it has been gone over many times. That’s what the nine o’clock class is for.

After Revelation 19 and Isaiah 63, now we know who the Word is. “In the beginning was the Word”: in the beginning was Christ. “And the Word was with God”: Christ was with God. “And the Word was God”: Christ was God. Christ was with God, then Christ was God: what does that mean? We can’t forget how we got here; we’re trying to find out why Christ is being called the everlasting Father.

The answers coming back about the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are very Christian. Now y’all understand why the Christians say what they say: when you don’t have an understanding you fall into that. Psalms 82 shows that somebody besides the Most High is called gods, and that brings us back to the fact that Christ is God.

precepts.why:
“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” There is the precept for the Word.

“His eyes were as a flame of fire”: we went over that already; y’all know who that is. “And on his head were many crowns”: because he shall be the King of kings and Lord of lords. When the Lord comes back he’s going to snatch everybody’s crown; now he’s the king of the earth, no question about it. “And he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.”

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood”: why does it say that? We read it in Genesis 49 as well, where he washed his garments in wine and his clothes in the blood of grapes. It’s mentioning it again here.

“Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save. Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” Remember how we make wine: you step on the grapes, and all of the juices fly up on you.

“I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me”: I went in there and did that work all by myself, nobody was with me. “For I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury”: who’s being trampled? Edom. “And their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments”.

That’s the vesture dipped in blood. Go back to Revelation 19:13: “And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” Now we know who the Word is: Christ. That’s how you’re going to be able to break this stuff down. Y’all sit around playing Assassin’s Creed; this is Apollos Creed.

sense.text:
“In the beginning was the Word”: in the beginning was Christ. “And the Word was with God”: Christ was with God. “And the Word was God”: Christ was God. Revelation 19 already told us his name is called the Word of God, so we know who the Word is.

It says Christ was with God, then it says Christ was God. What does that mean? Remember why we are here: we are trying to find out why Christ is being called the everlasting father. That sounds very Christian, and now you understand how the Christians speak and why they say what they say: when you don’t have an understanding, you fall into that. Christ is God, but somebody besides the Most High is being called gods, and there are levels.

Why is he called the everlasting father? We were created in his image, and when the wicked get wiped out we step forward in our promise; he is the father of the Israelites. But remember there’s another scripture that says we are going to be heirs unto him, that we are going to be adopted and be his brother. Everything has to be taken in context.

“All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” Who is the subject of the conversation? Christ. It is telling you plainly, but people are scared to say it, because we’ve been indoctrinated. Years and years of madness pumped into your mind, so even while we are reading it we’re not accepting it. That’s why we have to be born again, why the Lord said be like the child: get rid of all that stuff we learned and take it in new.

Christ was used to create everything. Christ literally created the thing; he did the work. That’s why he is being called everlasting father. The Most High is called the Most High God; Christ is called everlasting father because he created us. The Most High created him, and then he had to do his job.

precepts.why:
“God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” Who are these gods? The mighty is talking about Christ and his angels. What is that telling you? That somebody besides the Most High is being called gods.

Read on in the same chapter: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” “Defend the poor and fatherless: do justice to the afflicted and needy.” “They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness”, and then: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” So you Israelite men are also known as gods, but you’re going to die like men. There are levels.

So that brings us back to the fact that Christ is God: “the Word was God.”

sense.text:
This is one of those classes where you have to really think. Apollos used these scriptures to prove that Jesus was the Christ, and that’s some heavy stuff.

“But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.” Based on the precepts we know who that is. Remember Isaiah 9:6 calls him the everlasting father, and here it says “from everlasting.” “Whose goings forth have been from of old”: what did it say about Christ? He was there in the beginning. These are the scriptures that show Christ.

precepts.why:
“And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judea: for thus it is written by the prophet, And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” That is Micah 5:2, written by the prophet, and when you read Matthew 2 that’s when you go into the birth of Christ.

These things were being written based upon the prophecies. How do you think the wise men knew what to look for? Why would they be called the wise men? Because they were well studied in the scriptures; they knew what was to come. Always remember there was no New Testament. That’s why we’ve got to be sharp in both, because the New Testament is based on the old.

sense.text: “And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.” The people were complaining in the wilderness because they were eating manna. They said, ‘We hate this damned bread, man, we hate this bread.’ In Egypt they had all type of different food; it was like being in America, where you could go to the store and get all type of melons and fruits and vegetables and meats. Now they were out in the wilderness and the Lord was hitting them with this bread, and they hated it.
“And the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people”: fiery means fierce, attack serpents. “And they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.”

“Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.” He made it of brass and put it on a pole. You see that on the ambulances and next to the hospitals, that pole with the serpent going around it: that means health. After they were in that sin, the Lord said, look at this brass serpent and you are going to be healed.

What was this really going into? This is one of the scriptures Apollos could have used to show that Jesus was the Christ.

precepts.why:
“And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.” This is what Christ was teaching: he was saying this is what we are supposed to be looking at. It wasn’t written at the time of Apollos, but Numbers 21 was there.

“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son”: people read that and say he’s for everybody. But when Israelites are speaking to each other, they already know what this is talking about. The world is teaching madness.

This is what was there that Apollos could have used as well as Numbers 21. “For when the horrible fierceness of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, thy wrath endured not for ever”: this is the history we just read in Numbers 21 about the fiery serpents.

“But they were troubled for a small season”: who was troubled? The Israelites. “That they might be admonished”, that they might be corrected, “having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law”, so they could remember the commandments of God. We know that only Israel got the commandments. That’s what John 3:16 is talking about.

“For he that turned himself toward it”: the it is the brass serpent. He “was not saved by the thing that he saw”: nobody was saved by the brass serpent, “but by thee, that art the Saviour of all.” So it was already known that the serpent was going to be a foreshadowing and a representation of Christ, and this was around when Apollos was doing his thing. That’s why when they wrote John 3:16 they didn’t have to say ‘unto the Israelites’; everybody knew what it was. These are the scriptures we can use to teach: put it together precept upon precept.

sense.text:
When you see what Apollos did, that brother going through the scriptures pulling everything out and proving that Jesus was the Christ, that thing is crazy.

“He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.” What is that talking about? Out of thirty or forty brothers in the room, seven raised their hands to say they read the Gospels, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. That’s terrible, and that’s why you’re clueless to this day. It isn’t that you’ve got to know the exact scripture, but you should know something.

When he was on the cross, the soldier came to see if he was dead, and they didn’t break his legs. During the time of the crucifixion they would break your legs to assist in your death, but with Christ they didn’t do that, so he fulfilled something. It proves there was a prophecy. This is what the prophets knew; this is how those apostles and disciples were teaching and how they were able to make the people believe.

precepts.why:
“When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.” The Jews besought Pilate “that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.” “Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him”: there were two other brothers crucified with Christ. “But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water.”

“For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.” That is the scripture we just read in Psalms, and there is one in the book of Numbers as well, to show that even from way back in the time of Moses this was already being prophesied.

This is how these brothers broke it down; this is how they knew Christ was Christ. Some of the brothers walking with Christ weren’t even 100% believing: you have the brother named Thomas. The disciples went to the gravesite to anoint his body, although he told them he would be gone; they weren’t thinking it was actually going to happen. It wasn’t that Christ talked to them and they understood it right away. They learned over time, and they had to have faith.

“The fourteenth day of the second month at even they shall keep it, and eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.” Verse 11 is there to show it is the Passover. “They shall leave none of it unto the morning, nor break any bone of it: according to all the ordinances of the passover they shall keep it.”

What does the Passover have to do with Christ? Not a bone of the Passover was to be broken, the same as “A bone of him shall not be broken.”

“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. So Christ is the Passover. When he was crucified, no bones were broken: he has now become the Passover, the Lamb of God, and that is what Numbers 9 is telling you.

These are our precepts. These are the dark sayings that are able to make you understand the scriptures. This is how the Lord works.

sense.text: “They pierced my hands and my feet. I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me. They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.” When you read that, you’re not going to know what it is dealing with until the time of Christ. Then you understand it.
“For dogs have compassed me”: what is that talking about? The dogs are the other nations.

precepts.why:
“Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered unto him the whole band of soldiers. And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe.” They “put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him”. They were beating him and put the crown of thorns on him, and they bowed and said, ‘Yeah, King,’ but they were mocking him, because he was beaten up and bloody. “And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and smote him on the head.”

They “led him away to crucify him”, and compelled a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, to bear his cross, to “a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull”. “They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof, he would not drink.”

“And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.” That is what we just read in Psalms 22.

“I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” “Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me. But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” When you read up, it tells you she is not an Israelite. So Christ was calling the other nations dogs: it is not meet to take the children’s meat, the children of Israel’s gifts, and give it to the dogs.

“But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.” The last time we read dogs, it was the other nations; this one is talking about the Egyptians.

How do you know this dog is not a real dog? Dogs don’t talk, and this is about the tongue. And it says against man or beast. If it was a real dog, why would it say a dog won’t move his tongue against any man or beast? It is the other nations, meaning the Egyptians: they won’t have anything to say against the Israelites, the people or the animal.

That is how simple things are. We have to study; you can’t be out here looking crazy.
